audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.


Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo del 2.53%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.73%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.


Sul fronte dei mercati occidentali, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.58%, il VIX è in aumento dello 0.44%. L'oro è sopra i 4543 dollari l'oncia, in rialzo dello 0.99%, mentre il petrolio è in calo dell'1.13% a 92.65 dollari. Il rendimento del decennale USA è in calo dello 0.58% al 4.45%. Il DXY è in rialzo dello 0.11% a 99.13 L'STOXX 600 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.45%.


In ambito geopolitico, dichiarazioni del capo della banca centrale coreana suggeriscono che l'effetto del boom dell'AI sta compensando i timori legati alla guerra in Iran. Questo ha avuto un impatto sui mercati.


Sul fronte macro, oggi in uscita il PCE Core YoY negli USA. Il dato potrebbe fornire indicazioni importanti sull'inflazione.


Nessun altro dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantamila dollari, con una variazione del +0,48%. Tuttavia, i flussi ETF hanno registrato una significativa uscita di 733,4 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dinamiche di mercato.

Ethereum guadagna lo 0,93%, arrivando a duemilatrecento dollari, mentre Solana sale dell'1,55% a ottantadue dollari e tredici centesimi. BNB registra una crescita dello 0,35%, quotato a seicentotrentacinque dollari e novantacinque centesimi.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a 23, in zona di Extreme Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Outlook breve: oggi attenzione ai dati USA PCE Core YoY. 
  Per approfondire, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. 
  Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.

In Western markets, the S&P 500 closed up 0.58%, and the VIX rose 0.44%. Gold is trading above $4,543 per ounce, up 0.99%, while oil is down 1.13% at $92.65 The 10-year US yield is down 0.58% at 4.45%. The DXY is up 0.11% at 99.13 The STOXX 600 closed up 0.45%. Geopolitically, statements from the head of the Korean central bank suggest that the AI boom's effect is offsetting fears related to the war in Iran, impacting markets. On the macro front, the PCE Core YoY data is due out today in the US, which could provide important inflation insights. No other significant macro data is scheduled for release today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin remains above seventy thousand dollars, with a variation of +0.48%. However, ETF flows have seen a significant outflow of $733.4 million. This movement may be influenced by recent market dynamics. Ethereum gains 0.93%, reaching $2,300, while Solana rises 1.55% to $82.13 BNB registers a growth of 0.35%, quoted at $635.95 The Fear & Greed Index is at 23, in Extreme Fear territory, suggesting investor caution. Thank you for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: The strength of the inflation-output link in China
articles.snippet: by Mikael Juselius, Wenzhe Li We systematically investigate the relationship between China's inflation, economic slack, and expectations through the lens of New Keynesian Phillips Curves (NKPC). Extending existing research, we employ inflation expectations from Consensus Economics over recent samples and assess the stability of the estimates. Despite China's unique and evolving institutions, NKPC estimates are stable and show significant roles for both the output gap and inflation expectations in contrast to previous findings. Incorporating open-economy variables marginally enhances the models performance. Our results suggest that the New Keynesian framework can be adopted to China without adjustments for specific institutional features.

articles.title: Contriving Imaginary Gaps in Nuclear Deterrence
articles.snippet: Among some nuclear strategists, military officers, and lawmakers, a belief bordering on the canonical has taken root that the United States is on the short end of a “deterrence gap” with Russia and China. Both countries, and especially Russia, possess theater-range nuclear weapons, whose comparatively small yield is thought to lower the threshold for their use. The relative dearth of these capabilities on the American side, so the thinking goes, denies Washington the ability to answer a limited regional nuclear strike with a comparable response and thus deter such an attack in the first place. articles.title: BIS residential property price statistics, Q4 2025
articles.snippet: Real global house prices fell by 0.6% year on year (yoy) at the end of 2025. Real prices were almost stable in advanced economies (0.4% yoy), while they continued to decrease in emerging market economies (–1.4% yoy), especially in Asia. Since the outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic, real global house prices have increased by almost 3%. Among major jurisdictions, Türkiye, Australia and Mexico recorded the strongest increases, while prices in China and Canada were still below their pre-pandemic levels. From a longer-term perspective, real global house prices have increased by almost 20% since the end of the Great Financial Crisis (GFC) of 2007–09. articles.title: Reading Between China’s Red Lines
articles.snippet: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s blunt warning to US President Donald Trump about Taiwan was clearly intended to sharpen the distinction between this ultimatum and the many others Xi has issued. But expanding the number of non-negotiable positions reduces the space for effective diplomacy and raises the risk of accidental conflict.
